2.1 Key findings that drive the work:
1. Finance is the largest gap. Seven whole sections have no V10 menu (General Ledger, Inter Company, Taxation & Compliances, Inventory Financials, Fixed Assets, Migrations, GST Doc Integration). Most of the new V10 entries in this specification are in Finance Management.
2. Setup masters are the next gap. Many Sales, Product and Sourcing codes are not in the V10 mock and are proposed as new entries under the relevant Setups sub-menu.
3. Several transaction screens are missing from V10, including Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer and Update Pallet Location.
4. V10 adds 86 menus that Shahi does not have today (for example Supplier Onboarding, Audits, Recipes, Batch Traceability, Security & Access, Workflow & Approvals). Seven of them are marked "Removed in V10" and are excluded.
5. Many legacy menu rows are actions, not screens. Legacy entries named New, List, Search or Pending normally become buttons or tabs inside the parent page (see 6.3).

candidates.text:
3. Menu standards:
1. Three levels at most. A path is Module > Sub Menu > Page Name. Where the legacy structure was deeper, the levels in between are dropped and the page sits directly under the sub-menu.
2. The page name is the last level of the path. Column K must always equal the last part of column J. The page title shown on screen must use the same text.
3. List menus use the plural. A page that lists records is named in the plural (Suppliers, Seasons, Themes, Production Orders, PO Templates). Where the legacy name is plural, the V10 name must not be singular.
4. Separator format. Levels are separated by space, greater-than sign, space (" > "). No empty levels, no double spaces, no missing spaces.
5. Title case. Every word in a menu label starts with a capital letter except short joining words (of, for, to, and). Example: Payment Terms, not Payment terms.
6. One path, one page. Two different screens must not share the same full path. Where they do, one must be renamed (see 8.2).
7. Actions are not menu items. New, List, Search, Pending and similar entries become buttons or tabs inside the page and are controlled by action-level permissions.
8. No test, personal or note rows. Rows such as "Yudesh Sir" or requirement notes typed as menu rows must not be built.

candidates.text:
6.2 Navigation behaviour:
1. The menu must never show more than three levels. A Level 2 item opens its list of pages; it does not open a page itself.
2. The breadcrumb on every page reads Module > Sub Menu > Page Name, using exactly the text in the build list.
3. The browser tab title and the page heading use the Page Name.
4. A V10 path that appears under more than one legacy module (for example Reporting, or Sales > Setups > Payment Terms reached from Sourcing and Finance) is built once and shown once.
5. Menu search, where available, must index the Page Name and the legacy names in the Legacy menu IDs field, so users can still find a page by its old name during the transition.

6.3 Actions inside pages:
1. List and Search become the default view of the page (a list with search/filter).
2. New becomes a button on the list view that opens the entry form.
3. Other children with their own screen (for example Supplier Invoice Return List, Download Invoices, Update GL Date) keep their own V10 path as shown in Section 5.
4. Each action has its own permission key under the page Menu ID (for example FINANCE.AP.SUPPLIERINVOICE.NEW), so that rights held on the legacy New or List entries can be carried over exactly.

candidates.text:
6.7 Permissions:
1. A user sees a Page only if they hold its view permission. A Menu group is shown only if the user can see at least one page under it. An empty module is hidden.
2. Rights migrate from legacy menu IDs to V10 Menu IDs using Appendix A. Where several legacy entries merge into one V10 page, the user gets the page if they had any of the legacy entries; action rights are carried per action.
3. Dev must produce a migration report listing every user and role whose visible menu changes, for Implementation to review (7.1).
candidates.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions

candidates.text:
6.8 Acceptance criteria:
1. Every Page in Section 5 can be reached in no more than three clicks from the main menu.
2. No menu path has more than three levels and no two pages share a path.
3. Menu label, page title and breadcrumb match the build list exactly, including plural and capitalisation.
4. No New, List or Search entries appear as menu items; they are available as actions with working permissions.
5. Every legacy menu ID in Appendix A opens the correct V10 page.
6. A user migrated from a legacy role sees the same set of screens and actions as before, apart from changes approved in Section 8.
7. All items marked Confirm or Folder (review) have a recorded decision before release.
candidates.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.8 Acceptance criteria

candidates.text:
7.1 Roles and rights migration:
1. Export the current Shahi roles, users and their menu rights before the change.
2. Run the Dev migration (6.7) on a copy of production data.
3. Compare the before and after menu for each role using the Dev migration report. Investigate every role that loses or gains a screen.
4. Pay special attention to merged pages (Appendix A rows that share a V10 path) and to the Finance module, where most entries are new.
5. Get sign-off on the final role matrix from the customer process owners for each module.
candidates.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.1 Roles and rights migration

candidates.text:
7.2 User communication:
1. Publish a "Where did my menu go?" guide built from Appendix A, one page per legacy module, sorted by legacy menu name.
2. Explain the three main changes: menus renamed (for example Buyer to Customer), menus moved between modules (for example Sales ASN to Logistic, Material Requisitions to Sourcing), and New/List entries now being buttons inside the page.
3. Communicate module renames: Product → Products and Development, Production → Manufacturing, QC → Quality & Compliance, FA → Finance Management, Planning → Plan, TNA → Utilities > TNA, Admin → Administrators and Utilities.
candidates.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.2 User communication

7.4 User acceptance testing:
1. For each module, a key user opens every Page in Section 5 from the menu and confirms the right screen opens.
2. Test at least one legacy bookmark or link per module and confirm the redirect.
3. Test New, List and Search actions on merged pages with a user who had only one of the legacy rights.
4. Confirm role visibility for at least one user per role in the migration report.
5. Record defects against the Menu ID so Dev can trace them to the build list.
candidates.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.4 User acceptance testing

candidates.text:
7.5 Cut-over and rollback:
1. Freeze menu and role changes in Shahi from the agreed date until go-live.
2. Deploy the V10 menu configuration and run the rights migration in the agreed downtime window.
3. Smoke-test one page per module with a key user before releasing to all users.
4. Keep the legacy menu configuration and role export so the previous menu can be restored if a blocking defect is found.
5. Provide floor support for the first week, with the Appendix A guide at hand.

chunks.title: 1. Purpose and scope
chunks.heading: 1. Purpose and scope
chunks.text:
This specification defines the V10 menu that replaces the current Shahi menu. It turns the analysis in the source workbook into build instructions for the Development team and roll-out instructions for the Implementation team.
The scope covers every row of the 11 module sheets in the workbook (Product, Sales, Sourcing, Production, Inventory, QC, FA, Planning, TNA, Reports, Admin), together with the To Confirm and Excel Data Errors sheets. Screen behaviour inside each page is out of scope unless stated; this document is about where each screen sits in the menu, what it is called, how it is reached and who can see it.
chunks.locator: § 1. Purpose and scope

chunks.title: 1.1 How to read this document
chunks.heading: 1. Purpose and scope › 1.1 How to read this document
chunks.text:
• Section 2 summarises the gap between the legacy menu and the V10 HTML mock.
• Section 3 sets the naming and structure rules every menu entry must follow.
• Section 4 lists the corrections already applied to the Proposed Menu column.
• Section 5 is the target V10 menu, module by module. This is the build list.
• Sections 6 and 7 are the Development and Implementation requirements.
• Section 8 lists open decisions. Appendix A maps every legacy menu row to its V10 location.

chunks.title: 2.1 Key findings that drive the work
chunks.heading: 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work
chunks.text:
• Finance is the largest gap. Seven whole sections have no V10 menu (General Ledger, Inter Company, Taxation & Compliances, Inventory Financials, Fixed Assets, Migrations, GST Doc Integration). Most of the new V10 entries in this specification are in Finance Management.
• Setup masters are the next gap. Many Sales, Product and Sourcing codes are not in the V10 mock and are proposed as new entries under the relevant Setups sub-menu.
• Several transaction screens are missing from V10, including Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer and Update Pallet Location.
• V10 adds 86 menus that Shahi does not have today (for example Supplier Onboarding, Audits, Recipes, Batch Traceability, Security & Access, Workflow & Approvals). Seven of them are marked "Removed in V10" and are excluded.
• Many legacy menu rows are actions, not screens. Legacy entries named New, List, Search or Pending normally become buttons or tabs inside the parent page (see 6.3).
chunks.locator: § 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work

chunks.title: 3. Menu standards
chunks.heading: 3. Menu standards
chunks.text:
Every entry in the V10 menu must follow these rules. They were applied to the Proposed Menu column and are the acceptance rules for any later change.
• Three levels at most. A path is Module > Sub Menu > Page Name. Where the legacy structure was deeper, the levels in between are dropped and the page sits directly under the sub-menu.
• The page name is the last level of the path. Column K must always equal the last part of column J. The page title shown on screen must use the same text.
• List menus use the plural. A page that lists records is named in the plural (Suppliers, Seasons, Themes, Production Orders, PO Templates). Where the legacy name is plural, the V10 name must not be singular.
• Separator format. Levels are separated by space, greater-than sign, space (" > "). No empty levels, no double spaces, no missing spaces.
• Title case. Every word in a menu label starts with a capital letter except short joining words (of, for, to, and). Example: Payment Terms, not Payment terms.
• One path, one page. Two different screens must not share the same full path. Where they do, one must be renamed (see 8.2).
• Actions are not menu items. New, List, Search, Pending and similar entries become buttons or tabs inside the page and are controlled by action-level permissions.
chunks.locator: § 3. Menu standards

chunks.title: 3. Menu standards
chunks.heading: 3. Menu standards
chunks.text: • No test, personal or note rows. Rows such as "Yudesh Sir" or requirement notes typed as menu rows must not be built.
chunks.locator: § 3. Menu standards (part 2)

chunks.title: 6.1 Menu configuration record
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.1 Menu configuration record
chunks.text: Each row of the Section 5 build list becomes one menu configuration record. The record must hold the fields below. Fields marked "from workbook" are filled directly from the source workbook; the rest are set by Dev.
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.1 Menu configuration record

chunks.title: 6.1 Menu configuration record – Table 19
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.1 Menu configuration record
chunks.text:
Columns: Field (text); Description (text); Source (text)
Field | Description | Source
Menu ID | Unique, stable key. Proposed format MODULE.SUBMENU.PAGE in upper case with spaces removed (for example SOURCING.SETUPS.SUPPLIERS). | Dev
Level 1 – Module | First part of the V10 path. | From workbook (col J)
Level 2 – Sub Menu | Second part of the V10 path. Not clickable; opens the sub-menu. | From workbook (col J)
Level 3 – Page Name | Third part of the V10 path; also the page title and breadcrumb label. | From workbook (col K)
Node type | Menu group, Page or Folder (review). | Section 5
Technology | 1.0, 4.0 or Angular; decides how the page is opened (6.4). | From workbook (col I)
Target URL / route | Route of the existing legacy page, or of the new V10 page. | Dev
Legacy menu IDs | All legacy menu entries merged into this page; used for rights migration and redirects. | Appendix A
Sort order | Order within the sub-menu. Default: as in the V10 HTML mock; new items placed after existing ones alphabetically unless the Product Owner says otherwise. | Dev / PO
Actions | List of in-page actions (New, List, Search, Pending, Approve …) with their own permission keys. | Legacy child rows
Status | Existing, New or Confirm. | Section 5

chunks.title: 6.2 Navigation behaviour
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.2 Navigation behaviour
chunks.text:
• The menu must never show more than three levels. A Level 2 item opens its list of pages; it does not open a page itself.
• The breadcrumb on every page reads Module > Sub Menu > Page Name, using exactly the text in the build list.
• The browser tab title and the page heading use the Page Name.
• A V10 path that appears under more than one legacy module (for example Reporting, or Sales > Setups > Payment Terms reached from Sourcing and Finance) is built once and shown once.
• Menu search, where available, must index the Page Name and the legacy names in the Legacy menu IDs field, so users can still find a page by its old name during the transition.
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.2 Navigation behaviour

chunks.title: 6.3 Actions inside pages
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.3 Actions inside pages
chunks.text:
Legacy rows named New, List, Search, Pending and similar have been mapped to the same V10 path as their parent. Dev must not create these as menu items. Instead:
• List and Search become the default view of the page (a list with search/filter).
• New becomes a button on the list view that opens the entry form.
• Other children with their own screen (for example Supplier Invoice Return List, Download Invoices, Update GL Date) keep their own V10 path as shown in Section 5.
• Each action has its own permission key under the page Menu ID (for example FINANCE.AP.SUPPLIERINVOICE.NEW), so that rights held on the legacy New or List entries can be carried over exactly.
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.3 Actions inside pages

chunks.title: 6.4 Technology handling
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.4 Technology handling
chunks.text: The build list carries the legacy technology for each page. The menu must open the page in the correct way for that technology.
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.4 Technology handling

chunks.title: 6.5 New menu entries
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.5 New menu entries
chunks.text: 310 V10 paths are new. For each one Dev must create the menu record, link it to the existing legacy page (most new entries are existing Shahi screens that the V10 mock does not show yet) and apply the standards in Section 3. The largest blocks are Finance Management (141), Sales (30), Sourcing (25) and Products (23).
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.5 New menu entries

chunks.title: 6.6 Legacy links and redirects
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.6 Legacy links and redirects
chunks.text:
• Saved bookmarks, dashboard tiles, e-mail links and notifications that point to a legacy menu must keep working. Each legacy menu ID in Appendix A redirects to its V10 page.
• Where a legacy entry has become an action (New, List), the redirect opens the V10 page with that action selected.
• Legacy entries excluded from V10 (Section 8.4) redirect to the module home page with a short message.
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.6 Legacy links and redirects

chunks.title: 6.7 Permissions
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions
chunks.text:
• A user sees a Page only if they hold its view permission. A Menu group is shown only if the user can see at least one page under it. An empty module is hidden.
• Rights migrate from legacy menu IDs to V10 Menu IDs using Appendix A. Where several legacy entries merge into one V10 page, the user gets the page if they had any of the legacy entries; action rights are carried per action.
• Dev must produce a migration report listing every user and role whose visible menu changes, for Implementation to review (7.1).
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions

chunks.title: 6.8 Acceptance criteria
chunks.heading: 6. Development specification › 6.8 Acceptance criteria
chunks.text:
• Every Page in Section 5 can be reached in no more than three clicks from the main menu.
• No menu path has more than three levels and no two pages share a path.
• Menu label, page title and breadcrumb match the build list exactly, including plural and capitalisation.
• No New, List or Search entries appear as menu items; they are available as actions with working permissions.
• Every legacy menu ID in Appendix A opens the correct V10 page.
• A user migrated from a legacy role sees the same set of screens and actions as before, apart from changes approved in Section 8.
• All items marked Confirm or Folder (review) have a recorded decision before release.
chunks.locator: § 6. Development specification › 6.8 Acceptance criteria

chunks.title: 7.1 Roles and rights migration
chunks.heading: 7. Implementation specification › 7.1 Roles and rights migration
chunks.text:
• Export the current Shahi roles, users and their menu rights before the change.
• Run the Dev migration (6.7) on a copy of production data.
• Compare the before and after menu for each role using the Dev migration report. Investigate every role that loses or gains a screen.
• Pay special attention to merged pages (Appendix A rows that share a V10 path) and to the Finance module, where most entries are new.
• Get sign-off on the final role matrix from the customer process owners for each module.
chunks.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.1 Roles and rights migration

chunks.title: 7.2 User communication
chunks.heading: 7. Implementation specification › 7.2 User communication
chunks.text:
• Publish a "Where did my menu go?" guide built from Appendix A, one page per legacy module, sorted by legacy menu name.
• Explain the three main changes: menus renamed (for example Buyer to Customer), menus moved between modules (for example Sales ASN to Logistic, Material Requisitions to Sourcing), and New/List entries now being buttons inside the page.
• Communicate module renames: Product → Products and Development, Production → Manufacturing, QC → Quality & Compliance, FA → Finance Management, Planning → Plan, TNA → Utilities > TNA, Admin → Administrators and Utilities.
chunks.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.2 User communication

chunks.title: 7.4 User acceptance testing
chunks.heading: 7. Implementation specification › 7.4 User acceptance testing
chunks.text:
• For each module, a key user opens every Page in Section 5 from the menu and confirms the right screen opens.
• Test at least one legacy bookmark or link per module and confirm the redirect.
• Test New, List and Search actions on merged pages with a user who had only one of the legacy rights.
• Confirm role visibility for at least one user per role in the migration report.
• Record defects against the Menu ID so Dev can trace them to the build list.
chunks.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.4 User acceptance testing

chunks.title: 7.5 Cut-over and rollback
chunks.heading: 7. Implementation specification › 7.5 Cut-over and rollback
chunks.text:
• Freeze menu and role changes in Shahi from the agreed date until go-live.
• Deploy the V10 menu configuration and run the rights migration in the agreed downtime window.
• Smoke-test one page per module with a key user before releasing to all users.
• Keep the legacy menu configuration and role export so the previous menu can be restored if a blocking defect is found.
• Provide floor support for the first week, with the Appendix A guide at hand.
chunks.locator: § 7. Implementation specification › 7.5 Cut-over and rollback
